newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark retreat seen held at 2.8020.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark retreat seen held at 2.8020.

text.p: Sterling's retreat from early highs against the mark is expected to hold at the 2.8020 level in the near-term , said technical analysts.
A break below this support then finds a prop at the round-figure 2.80 marks level before testing a rising trendline around 2.7880 drawn from the pound's mid-March lows.
"Sterling/mark is expected to dip towards 2.8030/20 and then rally strongly and should see 2.85 pressed near-term," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.
The 2.8030/20 point is Friday's top in Europe and the base of a gap to Monday's European low, currently 2.8050 marks.
Sterling/mark upside is seen held at the earlier top of the round-figure 2.82 and then at the 4-1/2 year high of 2.8231 marks seen in mid-April.

Above here, the 2.8280-2.8320 marks support band which held in 1992 before sterling's crash in September of that year as well as the psychological 2.83 level is expected to provide tough resistance for a break higher.
Cable, meanwhile, continued to occupy tight ranges, supported at Friday's low of $1.6205 and blocked at Thursday's top of $1.6290.
"Support at the $1.6175 recent range bottom has once again limited sterling's decline, keeping the recovery trend from the $1.5860 low intact," said the technical team at Chase Investment Bank.
This range bottom also coincides with the rising trendline drawn from the 1.5850-60 low seen in mid-March.
Cable upside faces initial resistance at $1.6260, today's and Friday's highs, before Thursday's top at $1.6290.
Above here, progress is hindered by minor trendline resistance around $1.6360 then last week's high of $1.6395 before challenging April's peak of $1.6550, said analysts.
